entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Bartolomeo Visconti, also known as Bartolomeo Aicardi Visconti, was a Roman Catholic prelate of Italian descent, serving as Bishop of Novara from 1429 to 1457.

Born into a noble family, Visconti received a classical education and was ordained as a priest. He played a significant role in the governance of Novara, implementing reforms and promoting the welfare of the city's inhabitants.

Visconti's legacy extends beyond his tenure as Bishop, as he contributed to the development of the Catholic Church in Italy during the 15th century. His influence can be seen in the establishment of new institutions and the promotion of religious education.

In the years following his death, Visconti's life and work have been the subject of scholarly study, with many historians recognizing his importance as a key figure in the history of the Catholic Church in Italy.

The sheer weight of Visconti's legacy is best encapsulated in the words of the 16th-century historian, 'He was a man of great piety and learning, who left an enduring mark on the Church in Italy.'
